title: Different Groups of Numbers With a Given Sum

concept.title: Each number once, and equal numbers are one choice
body: Now every number can be used **at most once**, but the list can contain equal numbers, such as `1 1 2 3`. Two groups are the same if they have the same values (`{1, 2}` made with the first 1 or the second 1 counts once). The tools are the ones from the subset problem with repeats: **sort**, and at one step of the loop skip a value equal to the previous one.

Here the numbers are positive, so when `remaining` reaches 0 the group is complete and no larger group with this prefix can have the same sum: we return 1 at once. The loop condition `a[i] > remaining` is a pruning rule that works because the list is sorted.

statement: You are given `n` positive integers (some may be equal) and a target `t`. Count the different groups of numbers with sum `t`, where each position can be used at most once, and two groups are the same if they contain the same values with the same multiplicities.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.
outputFormat: Print the number of different groups.
hints: Sort the numbers and choose them in increasing order of index.
Skip a value that equals the previous one at the same step.
Stop the loop when a number is larger than what remains.

solution.complexity: Time proportional to the number of groups and partial groups, space O(n).
